The row's only witness, l1c26_rewrite_relative_invalid_key, uses a file USE procedure (USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON RELF). It never enables EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY checking and has no EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY declarative, so the case 2002 names has no evidence at 2002. My probe shows the compiler is correct at 2002. C2 (no INVALID KEY): the EC declarative runs (DECL=1), which follows §2002:9.1.12. 2023 gives the same output.

cases.reason: GR1 names the nested-table case explicitly. When identifier-1 is subordinate to an OCCURS, only identifier-1's index (and the VARYING operand) is modified, and the superordinate occurrence comes from the subscripts the user writes in the WHEN phrases. In 2002 that program has an UNSUBSCRIPTED identifier-1 (§2002 SR1). 2023 SR3 requires the superordinate subscripts on identifier-1, so a 2023 program of this case is not a 2002 program. This is the same cause the reader accepted for GR5 b). Neither row witness (ca36_search_range_dispatch, l1_search_no_at_end_no_checking) nor the extra tests the reader cited has a nested table: all are one-level OCCURS. So the nested arm of the 2002 rule has no evidence. My probe shows the compiler is correct at 2002: a Format 1 SEARCH INNR (unsubscripted) WHEN V (OX, IX) = 'G' with OX=2 finds IX=3 and leaves OX=2 and the second index IX2=3 unchanged. With OX=3 it takes AT END with OX unchanged.
